and this video walkthrough)."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## The Problem"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Open models (DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi) make the same tiny JSON mistakes in tool calls over and over"},{"id":"p8s2","text":". Each mistake triggers a validation error. The model retries with the same bad format. The session "},{"id":"p8s3","text":"degrades through 50+ wasted retry cycles. The model never learns because the error messages are opaq"},{"id":"p8s4","text":"rades through 50+ wasted retry cycles. The model never learns because the error messages are opaque."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"These mistakes are not random. They are a small finite set of patterns caused by the model's trainin"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"g distribution leaking through the tool boundary."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"### Harness vs Model"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"Most people frame this as a model problem: "DeepSeek is bad at tool calling, wait for the next versi"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"on." That is wrong. It is a **harness** problem. The harness sits between the model and the tool exe"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"cutor. It decides what to do with the model's output: reject it and waste tokens retrying, or fix it"},{"id":"p11s4","text":" silently and move on. A harness that repairs deterministically turns a bad-at-tool-calling model in"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"to a functional one in about 200 lines of code."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"The model did not change. | Bare string | `{"files": "main.ts"}` | `{"files": ["main.ts"]}` |
